import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Gourevitch's series identity

*References:*
 - [About a New Kind of Ramanujan-Type Series](https://doi.org/10.1080/10586458.2003.10504518) by *Jesús Guillera*
 - [G2003] Guillera, Jesús. "About a new kind of Ramanujan-type series." Experimental Mathematics 12.4 (2003): 507-510.
 - [A2025] Au, Kam Cheong. "Wilf-Zeilberger seeds and non-trivial hypergeometric identities." Journal of Symbolic Computation 130 (2025): 102421. [arXiv:2312.14051](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.14051)
-/

namespace Gourevitch


/-- The Gourevitch series identity:
The following identity holds:
$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{1 + 14 n + 76 n^2 + 168 n^3}{2^{20 n}} \binom{2n}{n}^7 = \frac{32}{\pi^3}.$
This was originally conjectured in [G2003] by Guillera and proven in [A2025] by Au.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 33]
theorem gourevitch_series_identity :
    ∑' n : ℕ, ((1 + 14 * n + 76 * n ^ 2 + 168 * n ^ 3) / (2 ^ (20 * n)) : ℝ)
      * Nat.centralBinom n ^ 7 = 32 / (Real.pi ^ 3) := by
  sorry

end Gourevitch

findings.description: The docstring says the identity was "originally conjectured in [G2003] by Guillera." The cited paper instead credits Boris Gourevitch with discovering it and communicating it to Guillera. This is only an attribution error; the Lean identity is faithful.
findings.source_evidence: Guillera, [G2003], §4, p. 509, immediately before equation (4–1): "Boris Gourevitch [Gourevitch 02] has sent me, by email, the formula below for 1/π³. He has found it by using integer relations algorithms." The bibliography identifies [Gourevitch 02] as a 2002 personal communication. Read at https://emis.dsd.sztaki.hu/journals/EM/expmath/volumes/12/12.4/Guillera.pdf. Au's introduction likewise attributes this formula to B. Gourevich.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the historical sentence with: "Conjectured by Boris Gourevitch and reported by Guillera in [G2003]; proved by Au in [A2025]." No change to the Lean statement is needed.

reformulations.difference: The sources express the summand using (1/2)_n^7/(n!)^7 and 2^(−6n), whereas Lean uses centralBinom n ^ 7 and 2^(−20n). Lean also states a `tsum` equality without a separate convergence assertion.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every n ≥ 0, (1/2)_n = binom(2n,n)·n!/4^n and (1)_n = n!. Thus the source summand equals P(n)·binom(2n,n)^7/2^(20n), where P(n)=168n³+76n²+14n+1. This termwise equality and the resulting series-equation equivalence were proved in the scratch file. Moreover, 32/π³ is nonzero, so the Lean equality cannot hold through `tsum`'s nonsummable default of zero: it is equivalent to `HasSum` with that value. All terms are positive, making `HasSum` equivalent to ordinary convergence of natural-indexed partial sums; this equivalence was also proved in Lean.

sources_consulted: Jesús Guillera, About a New Kind of Ramanujan-Type Series, Experimental Mathematics 12(4) (2003), 507–510, especially §4, equation (4–1): https://emis.dsd.sztaki.hu/journals/EM/expmath/volumes/12/12.4/Guillera.pdf

Kam Cheong Au, Wilf-Zeilberger seeds and non-trivial hypergeometric identities, arXiv:2312.14051v4, introduction and Example XI with its following remark; LaTeX source downloaded from https://arxiv.org/e-print/2312.14051
https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.14051 — version history and journal reference, J. Symbolic Comput. 130 (2025), 102421
review.notes: No mathematical misformalization or status issue found. The solved tag agrees with Au's cited proof. Lean experiments verified real-valued arithmetic, positive denominators, the n=0 term 1, and the n=1 term 259/8192.
